segments.text: Interviewer: So you started your singing career at a school talent show, didn't you? Singer: Yes, I did. I was only eight years old at the time, so I wasn't afraid to stand up and sing. I thought the audience would laugh, but they actually clapped and cheered. What a surprise that was. Interviewer: But you didn't try to start a singing career for a while, did you? Singer: No, I didn't. I was just interested in riding my bike and playing with my friends. People would ask me to sing for school shows, but I didn't think much of it at the time. Interviewer: You could sing a high C when you were 16 years old, couldn't you? Singer: Yes, I could. I was asked to sing our national song at a high school football game, and it had a high C. I practiced very hard, and I made it. After that, the recording studio in town asked me to record a CD. I tried it, and it sold a lot of copies. Interviewer: Your parents probably didn't want you to miss school, did they? Singer: Definitely not. But I could practice songs in my free time and record a CD during the school vacations. During the first summer after I started recording, I recorded three CDs in one summer. Interviewer: That was the summer you started selling CDs nationally, wasn't it? Singer: Yes, it was. Before that, I had only sold them near my hometown. When I started selling them nationally, I was surprised at the number I had sold. Interviewer: Folk music is your favorite, isn't it? Singer: Yes, it is. Soon, I hope to sing folk songs from other countries as well. Interviewer: It's been very nice to learn about your music. Do we get to hear you sing today? Singer: Certainly, I'd be happy to.
